warnings.filterwarnings(\"ignore\")\nimport h5py, numpy as np\nfrom dispersion.dmphasev2 import DMPhaseEstimator\nfrom flits.common.constants import K_DM\n\nF = \"/data/research/astrophysics/frbs/chime-dsa-codetections/chime_singlebeam/singlebeam_210456524.h5\"\nDM_C = 262.368\nDT = 2.56e-6\n\nwith h5py.File(F, \"r\") as h:\n    bb = h[\"tiedbeam_baseband\"]          # (nfreq, 2, ntime) complex64\n    freq = np.asarray(h[\"index_map\"][\"freq\"][\"centre\"], float)  # descending\n    I = (np.abs(bb[:, 0, :])**2 + np.abs(bb[:, 1, :])**2).astype(np.float64)  # (nfreq, ntime)\nprint(\"I shape\", I.shape, \"freq\", freq[0], \"->\", freq[-1])\n\n# incoherent dedisp at DM_c: shift each channel to align to top freq (numpy roll)\nref = freq.max()\ndelay_s = 1e-3 * K_DM * (1.0/freq**2 - 1.0/ref**2) * DM_C   # matches estimator's 1e-3*K_DM\nshift = np.round(delay_s / DT).astype(int)\n Idd = np.empty_like(I)\nfor j in range(I.shape[0]):\n    Idd[j] = np.roll(I[j], -shift[j])\nprof = np.nansum(Idd, axis=0)\npk = int(np.argmax(prof))\nprint(\"burst peak sample (dedisp@DM_c):\", pk, \"of\", I.shape[1])\n\n# window around the burst, downsample freq x2 for speed\nW = 1024\nlo, hi = max(pk - W, 0), min(pk + W, I.shape[1])\ndef run(Iwin, freqs, tag):\n    grid = np.arange(-4.0, 4.0, 0.1)         # RESIDUAL grid around 0 (data dedispersed @ DM_c)\n    est = DMPhaseEstimator(Iwin.T, freqs, DT, grid, ref=\"top\", n_boot=40, random_state=0)\n    c = est.result()[\"dm_curve\"]; b, s = est.get_dm(); ipk = int(np.argmax(c))\n    print(f\"  [{tag}] residual dm_best={b:+.3f}  sigma={s:.3f}  argmax_resid={grid[ipk]:+.2f}  \"\n          f\"interior={0<ipk<len(grid)-1}  -> CHIME_DM={DM_C+b:.3f}\")\n    return b, s\n\nfr2 = freq[::2]\nprint(\"forward orientation:\")\nrun(Idd[::2, lo:hi], fr2, \"fwd\")\nprint(\"time-flipped orientation:\")\nrun(Idd[::2, lo:hi][:, ::-1], fr2, \"flip\")\n\n# sign check: deliberately under-dedisperse by 1.0, expect residual to move by +/-1.0\nshift2 = np.round((1e-3*K_DM*(1.0/freq**2-1.0/ref**2)*(DM_C-1.0))/DT).astype(int)\nIdd2 = np.empty_like(I)\nfor j in range(I.shape[0]):\n    Idd2[j] = np.roll(I[j], -shift2[j])\nprint(\"under-dedispersed at DM_c-1.0 (expect residual peak to shift by ~+/-1.0):\")\nrun(Idd2[::2, lo:hi], fr2, \"fwd@DMc-1\")\nrun(Idd2[::2, lo:hi][:, ::-1], fr2, \"flip@DMc-1\")\n"
}

The probe reveals a real problem, not just a settings issue: the DM-structure peak **wanders with orientation and offset** (argmax +2.4 fwd / −2.4 flip; jumps to ∓3.2 when I under-dedisperse by 1.0) instead of tracking dispersion, and `dm_best` is stuck at the degenerate fallback (−0.5, σ=grid-step) in every case. That's the signature of **no clean structure peak** — expected if these scattered bursts have smooth profiles (scattering removes the sharp sub-structure that structure-DM needs). Before deciding, I need to *see* zach: is there sub-structure my coarse settings missed, or is it a smooth scattered blob? Let me make a diagnostic figure.

> AGENT

The zach figure is the key diagnostic: the waterfall is **blank** and the collapsed profile is **noise-like with no clean pulse**. That's not a settings problem — it's physics I can now quantify. Intra-channel dispersion smearing at CHIME's bottom band for zach (DM≈262):

t_intra ≈ 8.3×10⁶ ms × DM × Δν_chan / ν³ = 8.3e6 × 262 × 0.39 / 400³ ≈ **13 ms** per channel.

My host shortcut used only *incoherent* (integer-sample) dedispersion, which cannot remove that 13 ms intra-channel smear — so the low channels wash out entirely and structure-DM is hopeless. **Coherent dedispersion (docker) is mandatory** — exactly the path the plan originally specified and that the prior TOA work already validated bit-exactly. My deviation to a host-only approach was the mistake.

Let me record this course-correction in the plan and note the deviation, then build the extraction on the validated docker dedispersion path.

{
  "file_path": "/data/research/astrophysics/frbs/chime-dsa-codetections/scripts/diag_zach_docker.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Docker diagnostic (zach): is the burst clean once coherent dedispersion removes\nintra-channel smear? Mirrors the validated TOA-extraction dedispersion path.\nRun: bin/baseband_analysis_python.sh scripts/diag_zach_docker.py\n\"\"\"\nimport os\nos.environ.setdefault(\"MPLCONFIGDIR\", \"/tmp/mpl\")\nimport numpy as np\nimport matplotlib\nmatplotlib.use(\"Agg\")\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nfrom baseband_analysis.core.bbdata import BBData\nfrom baseband_analysis.core.dedispersion import coherent_dedisp, incoherent_dedisp\n\nROOT = \"/data/research/astrophysics/frbs/chime-dsa-codetections\"\nF = ROOT + \"/chime_singlebeam/singlebeam_210456524.h5\"\nOUT = ROOT + \"/diagnostics/diag_zach_docker.png\"\nDM_C = 262.368\n\nbb = BBData.from_file(F)\ndt = float(bb.attrs[\"delta_time\"])\nfreq = np.asarray(bb.index_map[\"freq\"][\"centre\"], float)\nprint(\"freq\", round(freq[0], 1), \"->\", round(freq[-1], 1), \"dt\", dt, flush=True)\n\n# (a) coherent dedisp only (intra-channel removed, inter-channel sweep kept)\nbb_coh = coherent_dedisp(bb, DM_C, time_shift=False)\nbb[\"tiedbeam_baseband\"][:] = bb_coh\nI_coh = np.abs(bb_coh[:, 0, :]) ** 2 + np.abs(bb_coh[:, 1, :]) ** 2  # (nfreq, ntime)\n\n# (b) + incoherent dedisp (fully aligned, as TOA script)\nbb_inc, _f, _fid = incoherent_dedisp(bb, DM_C, fill_wfall=True)\nI_inc = np.abs(bb_inc[:, 0, :]) ** 2 + np.abs(bb_inc[:, 1, :]) ** 2\n\n\ndef norm_and_window(I, half=1536):\n    coarse = np.nansum(np.nan_to_num(I), axis=0)\n    pk = int(np.nanargmax(coarse))\n    off = np.ones(I.shape[1], bool)\n    off[max(pk - 3000, 0) : pk + 3000] = False\n    mu = np.nanmean(I[:, off], axis=1, keepdims=True)\n    sd = np.nanstd(I[:, off], axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-9\n    In = np.nan_to_num((I - mu) / sd)\n    lo, hi = max(pk - half, 0), min(pk + half, I.shape[1])\n    return In[:, lo:hi], pk, (np.arange(hi - lo) - (pk - lo)) * dt * 1e3\n\n\nfig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 9))\nfor col, (I, tag) in enumerate([(I_coh, \"coherent only (intra removed)\"),\n                                 (I_inc, \"coherent+incoherent (aligned)\")]):\n    win, pk, t_ms = norm_and_window(I)\n    prof = np.nansum(win, axis=0)\n    nf = win.shape[0] // 4 * 4\n    disp = win[:nf].reshape(nf // 4, 4, win.shape[1]).mean(1)\n    ax[0, col].imshow(disp, aspect=\"auto\", origin=\"lower\",\n                      extent=[t_ms[0], t_ms[-1], freq[-1], freq[0]], vmin=-0.5, vmax=5, cmap=\"magma\")\n    ax[0, col].set(title=f\"zach {tag}\", ylabel=\"freq (MHz)\"); ax[0, col].set_xlim(-6, 14)\n    snr = prof.max() / prof[: len(prof) // 6].std()\n    ax[1, col].plot(t_ms, prof, lw=0.8, color=\"0.2\")\n    ax[1, col].set(title=f\"profile  snr~{snr:.1f}\", xlabel=\"t (ms)\"); ax[1, col].set_xlim(-6, 14)\n    print(f\"{tag}: peak@{pk} snr~{snr:.1f}\", flush=True)\nfig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(OUT, dpi=110)\nprint(\"wrote\", OUT, flush=True)\n"
}

Now zach is crystal clear: a **scattered pulse with a sharp rising edge and exponential tail** (right panel, aligned). The left panel (coherent-only) shows the burst still *sweeps* across the band — which is exactly what DM-phase needs to optimize against. So the recipe is: `coherent_dedisp(time_shift=False)` (intra-channel removed, sweep retained) → DM-phase with an absolute grid at DM_c. There's a real sharp leading edge, so structure-DM is defined (though a scattered single pulse will have larger σ than a multi-component burst).

I still need to nail the sign/centering on real data. Let me vendor a standalone DM-phase (no `flits` in the image) and run it in docker on zach, both orientations, to pin the recipe before the 12-burst run.

> AGENT

Now I have real signal and two key findings:

1. **Sign recipe**: the **time-flipped** orientation gives an interior peak (zach → 264.3, i.e. +1.9 from catalog — physically sensible, since structure-DM > S/N-DM for scattered "sad-trombone" bursts); forward rails to the low edge.
2. **`DMPhaseEstimator.get_dm()` is unreliable here**: its quadratic vertex-fit returned the grid edge with σ=0 (degenerate) even though the curve argmax is interior. The curve is shallow (12% modulation) for this scattered single pulse, so I need a **robust peak extraction** (argmax + bootstrap-argmax σ), not the quadratic vertex.

There's also a compute scaling problem: high-DM bursts (mahi DM 960) have ~18 ms dispersion sweeps → huge windows for the swept approach. The tractable fix is to **align first** (coherent+incoherent) then run DM-phase on a small **residual** grid around 0 in a tight window (works for all DMs). Let me validate that residual recipe + robust peak on zach in one quick docker probe before building the 12-burst run.

Found the bug: `incoherent_dedisp(fill_wfall=True)` returns a **1024-channel filled waterfall**, not the 871 of `index_map` — so my `freq` array (871) didn't match `I` (1024 → `[::2]`=512). The fix: avoid the channel-changing incoherent path. Use the coherent-only waterfall (871 ch, matches `freq`) and align with a numpy roll for windowing; DM-phase still does the fine residual search. Let me rewrite the probe that way.

  "old_string": "def position_consistent(dsa_coord: str, chime_center: str, radius_deg: float) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True if the DSA (arcsec) position lies within ``radius_deg`` of the CHIME disk centre.\"\"\"\n    import astropy.units as u\n    from astropy.coordinates import SkyCoord\n\n    a = SkyCoord(dsa_coord, unit=(u.hourangle, u.deg), frame=\"icrs\")\n    b = SkyCoord(chime_center, unit=(u.hourangle, u.deg), frame=\"icrs\")\n    return bool(a.separation(b).deg <= radius_deg)",
  "new_string": "def position_agreement(dsa_coord: str, chime_ra_deg, chime_dec_deg, radius_deg: float) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"CHIME tied-beam point vs DSA position; consistent within a stated CHIME radius.\n\n    ``tiedbeam_locations`` is the CHIME position the singlebeam was formed at (independent\n    of DSA) but carries no error ellipse, so consistency is judged against a stated CHIME\n    localization radius (assumption; Michilli et al. 2021 baseband localizations sub-arcmin).\n    Null+reason when no CHIME position is available.\n    \"\"\"\n    if chime_ra_deg is None or chime_dec_deg is None:\n        return {\n            \"separation_deg\": None,\n            \"radius_deg\": radius_deg,\n            \"consistent\": None,\n            \"reason\": \"no CHIME position available\",\n        }\n    import astropy.units as u\n    from astropy.coordinates import SkyCoord\n\n    a = SkyCoord(dsa_coord, unit=(u.hourangle, u.deg), frame=\"icrs\")\n    b = SkyCoord(chime_ra_deg, chime_dec_deg, unit=u.deg, frame=\"icrs\")\n    sep = float(a.separation(b).deg)\n    return {\n        \"separation_deg\": sep,\n        \"radius_deg\": radius_deg,\n        \"consistent\": bool(sep <= radius_deg),\n        \"reason\": None,\n    }"
}

46	    bb = BBData.from_file(path)
47	    dt = float(bb.attrs["delta_time"])
48	    freq = np.asarray(bb.index_map["freq"]["centre"], float)  # 871, descending
49	    ref = freq.max()
50	    ra = float(np.asarray(bb["tiedbeam_locations"]["ra"]).ravel()[0])
51	    dec = float(np.asarray(bb["tiedbeam_locations"]["dec"]).ravel()[0])
52	
53	    bb_coh = coherent_dedisp(bb, dm_c, time_shift=False)
54	    I = np.abs(bb_coh[:, 0, :]) ** 2 + np.abs(bb_coh[:, 1, :]) ** 2  # (871, ntime) intra-removed
55	    shift = np.round((1e-3 * K_DM * (1.0 / freq**2 - 1.0 / ref**2) * dm_c) / dt).astype(int)
56	    Idd = np.stack([np.roll(I[j], -s) for j, s in enumerate(shift)])  # roll-align @ DM_c
57	    pk = int(np.nanargmax(np.nansum(np.nan_to_num(Idd), 0)))
58	    lo, hi = max(pk - W, 0), min(pk + W, I.shape[1])
59	
60	    fr = freq[::FDS]
61	    win = np.nan_to_num(Idd[::FDS, lo:hi])
62	    # per-channel off-pulse normalize (robust display + downweights dead channels)
63	    half = win.shape[1] // 2
64	    off = np.r_[np.arange(0, half // 2), np.arange(win.shape[1] - half // 2, win.shape[1])]
65	    mu = win[:, off].mean(1, keepdims=True)
66	    sd = win[:, off].std(1, keepdims=True) + 1e-9
67	    wn = (win - mu) / sd
68

70	    curve = est.result()["dm_curve"]
71	    i = int(np.argmax(curve))
72	    bs_peaks = GRID[np.argmax(est._bs_curves, axis=1)]
73	    dm_chime = float(dm_c + GRID[i])
74	    dm_err = float(np.std(bs_peaks, ddof=1))
75	    interior = bool(0 < i < len(GRID) - 1)
76	    flat = float(curve.max() / curve.min())
77	    prof = wn.sum(0)
78	    snr = float(prof.max() / prof[off].std())

94	    ax[1].set(title=f"profile  snr~{snr:.1f}", xlabel="t (ms)")

def test_report_with_real_chime_inputs_activates_pillars():
    # the committed CHIME-side extraction (figure-reviewed): 11/12 DM active (isha=noise->null),
    # all 12 positions consistent, 3 real-confidence (zach/freya/casey)
    chime = ROOT / "crossmatching/chime_side_inputs.json"
    if not chime.exists():
        import pytest

        pytest.skip("chime_side_inputs.json not present")
    report = build_association_report(
        ROOT / "crossmatching/notebook_reproduction_fixture.json", chime_inputs_path=chime
    )
    by = {b["name"]: b for b in report["bursts"]}
    assert by["isha"]["dm_confidence"] == "noise"
    assert by["isha"]["dm_agreement"]["consistent"] is None  # railed -> nulled, not fabricated
    dm_active = [b for b in report["bursts"] if b["dm_agreement"]["consistent"] is not None]
    assert len(dm_active) == 11
    assert all(b["dm_agreement"]["consistent"] is True for b in dm_active)  # all within 3 sigma
    assert all(b["position"]["consistent"] is True for b in report["bursts"])  # 12/12 positions
    assert {b["name"] for b in report["bursts"] if b["dm_confidence"] == "real"} == {
        "zach",
        "freya",
        "casey",
    }

def _load_chime_inputs(chime_inputs_path) -> dict:
    """Index CHIME-side extraction rows by chime_id (empty dict if path absent/None)."""
    if not chime_inputs_path or not Path(chime_inputs_path).exists():
        return {}
    rows = json.loads(Path(chime_inputs_path).read_text())
    return {str(r["chime_id"]): r for r in rows if "dm_chime" in r}


def build_association_report(
    fixture_path,
    *,
    rate_per_day: float = 1000.0,
    omega_win_deg2: float = OMEGA_WIN_BASELINE_DEG2,
    dt_s: float = DT_BASELINE_S,
    ddm: float = DDM_BASELINE,
    chime_inputs_path=None,
    chime_radius_deg: float = 0.1,
) -> dict:
    """Run all four pillars over the fixture and return the report dict. Read-only on disk.

    Pillars 2 (CHIME DM) and 4 (CHIME position) activate per burst when a CHIME-side inputs
    file is supplied (``chime_inputs_path``, keyed by chime_id); bursts absent from it emit
    explicit null+reason rather than fabricated values.
    """
    fx = json.loads(Path(fixture_path).read_text())
    chime = _load_chime_inputs(chime_inputs_path)
    bursts, dms = [], []
    for row in fx["bursts"]:
        dm = row["dm"]
        dms.append(dm)
        ci = chime.get(str(row["chime_id"]), {})
        bursts.append(
            {
                "name": row["name"],
                "chime_id": row["chime_id"],
                "dm": dm,
                "chance_coincidence_P": chance_probability(
                    dm, rate_per_day=rate_per_day, omega_win_deg2=omega_win_deg2, dt_s=dt_s, ddm=ddm
                ),
                "dm_agreement": dm_agreement(
                    dm_chime=ci.get("dm_chime"),
                    dm_chime_err=ci.get("dm_chime_err"),
                    dm_dsa=dm,
                    dm_dsa_err=row.get("dm_uncertainty"),
                ),
                "dm_confidence": ci.get("dm_confidence"),  # figure-review: real/marginal/noise
                "position": position_agreement(
                    row.get("source_coord"),
                    ci.get("chime_ra_deg"),
                    ci.get("chime_dec_deg"),
                    chime_radius_deg,
                ),
            }
        )
    return {
        "inputs": {
            "rate_per_day": rate_per_day,
            "omega_win_deg2": omega_win_deg2,
            "dt_s": dt_s,
            "ddm": ddm,
            "dm_model": "lognormal(500,0.7) [assumption]",
            "chime_dm_method": "DM-phase structure-max (dmphasev2); coherent dedisp, flip orient",
            "chime_localization_radius_deg": chime_radius_deg,
            "chime_localization_note": "tiedbeam pointing; no multi-beam error ellipse "
            "(Michilli+2021 sub-arcmin assumed)",
        },
        "expected_chance_associations": expected_chance_associations(
            dms, rate_per_day=rate_per_day, omega_win_deg2=omega_win_deg2, dt_s=dt_s, ddm=ddm
        ),
        "bursts": bursts,
    }


def main() -> None:
def main() -> None:
    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    chime_path = here / "chime_side_inputs.json"
    chime_path = here / "chime_side_inputs.json"

    out = here / "association_report.json"
    out = here / "association_report.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(rep, indent=2))
    out.write_text(json.dumps(rep, indent=2))
    n_dm = sum(1 for b in rep["bursts"] if b["dm_agreement"]["consistent"] is not None)
    n_dm = sum(1 for b in rep["bursts"] if b["dm_agreement"]["consistent"] is not None)
    print(f"wrote {out}  (sum_mu={rep['expected_chance_associations']:.3e}, dm_active={n_dm}/12)")
    print(f"wrote {out}  (sum_mu={rep['expected_chance_associations']:.3e}, dm_active={n_dm}/12)")

That's a clean example. In **casey's left panel** you can see the bright track running **top-left → bottom-right**: high frequencies (top, ~750 MHz) arrive *earlier* (left, ~−1 ms), low frequencies (bottom, ~400 MHz) arrive *later* (right). That diagonal tilt is exactly the residual-dispersion signature.

Why it's there (and benign): the waterfall is roll-aligned at `DM_c` (the DSA DM) using **integer-sample shifts**. casey's true CHIME DM (493.0) sits ~1.8 units above `DM_c` (491.2), so a small residual sweep remains — and that residual is precisely what the DM-phase residual grid in panel 3 fits (its peak lands at +1.8 from `DM_c`). The tilt isn't misalignment; it's the few-DM-unit residual the method is designed to measure. A *full* band sweep across the whole window would signal a broken alignment — what you see is only a fraction of the window, consistent with a ~1–2 unit residual.

Other visible-sweep examples if you want to compare: `hamilton_dmphase.png` (narrow track, longer sweep), `chromatica_dmphase.png` (fainter), `zach_dmphase.png` (compact knot, least tilt — lowest DM). All in the same dir:

mahi and zach confirm it — and it's worse than a tilt. Look at **panel 3 across all four**: the DM-phase curves are *oscillatory, near-flat* (flat_ratio 1.2–1.5 = noise wiggles, not a coherence peak — a real structure-DM detection peaks sharply, ratio ≫1). The code just takes the global argmax of a noisy curve. And **panel 1**: zach and mahi are essentially pure noise (no burst at all); casey/hamilton show an *un-straightened* sweep. Even the two I called "real" are noise-dominated. You're right: the fits are bad across the board, and the σ's are small only because the noise pattern is stable across bootstraps — not because there's a real peak.

**Implication I have to own:** the Pillar-2 DM result I merged in PR #29 is compromised — likely DM-phase fitting noise. Pillar-4 (positions, from `tiedbeam_locations`) is independent and still valid. The merged Pillar-2 claims need correcting/reverting on main once we know the truth.

Leading root-cause hypothesis (must confirm, not assert): the extraction uses `coherent_dedisp(bb, dm_c, time_shift=False)` (intra-channel only) **then a hand-rolled inter-channel shift** — and that shift carries a `1e-3 * K_DM` factor that, with freq in MHz, is ~1000× too small. So the inter-channel dispersion is barely removed, the burst sweeps out of the few-ms window, and the "DM-phase curve" is computed on noise. The recovery test passed only because it dispersed *and* de-dispersed with the same wrong constant — it never checked absolute physical scaling.

> AGENT

**Root cause nailed — and it's in repo code, not just the off-repo script.** `flits.common.constants.K_DM = 4148.808` is already in **seconds** convention (its own comment says `MHz^2 pc^-1 cm^3 s`), but `dmphasev2.py:57` multiplies it by `1e-3`, making every dispersive delay **exactly 1000× too small**. That's why no curve ever peaked: the de-dispersion phase ramp was 1000× too weak to remove real dispersion. The fix is to delete `1e-3 *`. The recovery test never caught it because it injected dispersion with the same wrong factor.

Let me do P1 (test-first): read both files, fix line 57, rewrite the recovery test to inject *physical* dispersion and assert a sharply-peaked recovery.

1	"""DM-phase (structure-max) estimator must recover a known injected DM.
2	
3	Gate for the CHIME-side pillar-2 extraction: before trusting `DMPhaseEstimator`
4	on real bursts, prove it recovers the DM of a synthetic dispersed multi-component
5	waterfall to within its bootstrap uncertainty, with the peak *interior* to the grid
6	(a railed edge result must FAIL). Pure host test (no docker).
7	
8	Sign convention: `DMPhaseEstimator` de-disperses with phase
9	``exp(-2j pi f * DM * delay_sec)`` (dmphasev2.py:77), so its coherent power peaks at
10	positive DM for an injection whose per-channel delay carries the SAME sign as the
11	estimator's ``delay_sec`` correction (i.e. ``-K_DM*DM*(1/f^2 - 1/f_ref^2)`` here).
12	This fixes the test's injection orientation; the matching orientation for *real*
13	(physically dispersed) CHIME waterfalls is asserted empirically in the extraction
14	(it requires an interior peak and flips the time axis otherwise).
15	"""
16	
17	import numpy as np
18	
19	from dispersion.dmphasev2 import DMPhaseEstimator
20	from flits.common.constants import K_DM
21	
22	
23	def _disperse(n_t, freqs, dt, dm, comps):
24	    """Synthesize an intensity waterfall (n_t, n_ch) with sharp dispersed sub-pulses.
25	
26	    Delay uses the estimator's de-dispersion sign so a positive trial-DM grid recovers ``dm``.
27	    """
28	    ref = freqs.max()
29	    delay = -1e-3 * K_DM * (1.0 / freqs**2 - 1.0 / ref**2) * dm  # seconds, per channel
30	    t = np.arange(n_t) * dt
31	    wf = np.zeros((n_t, freqs.size))
32	    for t0, amp, width in comps:
33	        wf += amp * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t[:, None] - t0 - delay[None, :]) / width) ** 2)
34	    return wf
35	
36	
37	def test_dmphase_recovers_known_dm():
38	    # kept small on purpose: DM-phase allocates ~(n_grid, n_t, n_ch) per bootstrap,
39	    # so cost ~ n_grid*n_t*n_ch*n_boot — fine here, OOM-thrashes at notebook sizes.
40	    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
41	    freqs = np.linspace(400.0, 800.0, 96)
42	    dt, n_t, dm_true = 5.0e-4, 768, 500.0
43	    comps = [(0.18, 1.0, 1.0e-3), (0.186, 0.7, 1.0e-3)]  # two sharp sub-pulses, ~6 ms apart
44	    wf = _disperse(n_t, freqs, dt, dm_true, comps)
45	    wf += 0.05 * rng.standard_normal((n_t, freqs.size))
46	
47	    grid = np.arange(dm_true - 6.0, dm_true + 6.0, 0.2)
48	    est = DMPhaseEstimator(wf, freqs, dt, grid, ref="top", n_boot=40, random_state=1)
49	    dm_best, dm_sigma = est.get_dm()
50	
51	    # peak must be interior to the grid (a railed edge result is not a recovery)
52	    i_pk = int(np.argmax(est.result()["dm_curve"]))
53	    assert 0 < i_pk < len(grid) - 1, f"DM-structure peak railed to grid edge (idx {i_pk})"
54	    assert dm_sigma > 0
55	    assert abs(dm_best - dm_true) < max(3.0 * dm_sigma, 2.0 * (grid[1] - grid[0]))
56

  "content": "\"\"\"DM-phase (structure-max) estimator must recover a known injected DM — at PHYSICAL scale.\n\nGate for the CHIME-side pillar-2 extraction: before trusting `DMPhaseEstimator` on real\nbursts, prove it recovers the DM of a synthetic dispersed multi-component waterfall AND that\nits coherence curve actually *peaks* sharply (a near-flat curve is not a detection).\n\nPhysical-scale guard: the injection uses the real dispersion law\n``delay[s] = K_DM * DM * (1/f^2 - 1/f_ref^2)`` with K_DM in seconds (MHz^2 pc^-1 cm^3 s) and\nf in MHz — the SAME constant the estimator uses (dmphasev2.py:57). A regression that rescales\nthe estimator's delay (e.g. the old spurious 1e-3 factor, 1000x too small) breaks de-dispersion:\nthe curve goes flat and recovery fails, so this test catches it. Pure host test (no docker).\n\nSign convention: the estimator de-disperses with ``exp(-2j pi f * DM * delay_sec)``\n(dmphasev2.py:77), so a positive trial-DM grid recovers ``dm`` for an injection whose\nper-channel delay carries the estimator's sign, ``-K_DM*DM*(1/f^2 - 1/f_ref^2)``.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom dispersion.dmphasev2 import DMPhaseEstimator\nfrom flits.common.constants import K_DM\n\n\ndef _disperse(n_t, freqs, dt, dm, comps):\n    \"\"\"Synthesize an intensity waterfall (n_t, n_ch) with sharp PHYSICALLY-dispersed sub-pulses.\"\"\"\n    ref = freqs.max()\n    delay = -K_DM * (1.0 / freqs**2 - 1.0 / ref**2) * dm  # seconds, physical scale\n    t = np.arange(n_t) * dt\n    wf = np.zeros((n_t, freqs.size))\n    for t0, amp, width in comps:\n        wf += amp * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t[:, None] - t0 - delay[None, :]) / width) ** 2)\n    return wf\n\n\ndef test_dmphase_recovers_known_dm():\n    # cost ~ n_grid*n_t*n_ch*n_boot; kept modest. dm_true=20 -> ~0.39 s sweep across 400-800 MHz,\n    # comfortably inside the n_t*dt = 1.024 s window.\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)\n    freqs = np.linspace(400.0, 800.0, 96)\n    dt, n_t, dm_true = 1.0e-3, 1024, 20.0\n    comps = [(0.45, 1.0, 2.0e-3), (0.462, 0.7, 2.0e-3)]  # two sharp sub-pulses, ~12 ms apart\n    wf = _disperse(n_t, freqs, dt, dm_true, comps)\n    wf += 0.05 * rng.standard_normal((n_t, freqs.size))\n\n    grid = np.arange(dm_true - 5.0, dm_true + 5.0, 0.2)\n    est = DMPhaseEstimator(wf, freqs, dt, grid, ref=\"top\", n_boot=40, random_state=1)\n    curve = est.result()[\"dm_curve\"]\n\n    # peak must be interior to the grid (a railed edge result is not a recovery)\n    i_pk = int(np.argmax(curve))\n    assert 0 < i_pk < len(grid) - 1, f\"DM-structure peak railed to grid edge (idx {i_pk})\"\n\n    # the curve must actually PEAK: a working physical-scale estimator gives a sharp coherence\n    # peak; the 1000x-too-small delay regression gives a near-flat curve (ratio ~ 1).\n    flat_ratio = float(curve.max() / curve.min())\n    assert flat_ratio > 2.0, f\"DM-phase curve is near-flat (ratio {flat_ratio:.2f}) — no real peak\"\n\n    # robust recovery: argmax of the mean curve within ~2 grid steps of truth\n    dm_best = float(grid[i_pk])\n    assert abs(dm_best - dm_true) < 2.0 * (grid[1] - grid[0]), f\"dm_best={dm_best} != {dm_true}\"\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"P2 prototype: corrected CHIME structure-DM extraction on zach.\n\nRebuild on library dedispersion (no hand-rolled inter-channel roll, no 1e-3 bug):\n  coherent_dedisp(bb, dm_c)            # proper, time_shift=True -> clean vertical burst (zach SNR~15)\n  -> band-collapse, find burst, tight window\n  -> DMPhaseEstimator on a PHYSICAL residual-DM grid around 0 (data already at dm_c)\n  -> REQUIRE a sharp interior peak (flat_ratio >> noise floor), else 'no structure-DM'.\n\nValidation target: a clean vertical burst in panel 1 AND a sharply peaked DM-phase curve in panel 3.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nos.environ.setdefault(\"MPLCONFIGDIR\", \"/tmp/mpl\")\nsys.path.insert(0, \"/data/research/astrophysics/frbs/chime-dsa-codetections/scripts\")\nimport matplotlib\n\nmatplotlib.use(\"Agg\")\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\nfrom baseband_analysis.core.bbdata import BBData\nfrom baseband_analysis.core.dedispersion import coherent_dedisp\nfrom dmphase_standalone import DMPhaseEstimator\n\nROOT = \"/data/research/astrophysics/frbs/chime-dsa-codetections\"\nPATH = ROOT + \"/chime_singlebeam/singlebeam_210456524.h5\"  # zach\nDM_C = 262.368\n\nbb = BBData.from_file(PATH)\ndt = float(bb.attrs[\"delta_time\"])\nfreq = np.asarray(bb.index_map[\"freq\"][\"centre\"], float)  # 871 descending\nref = freq.max()\n\n# (1) proper coherent dedispersion -> intensity\nbbdd = coherent_dedisp(bb, DM_C)\nI = np.abs(bbdd[:, 0, :]) ** 2 + np.abs(bbdd[:, 1, :]) ** 2  # (871, ntime)\n\n# (2) RFI/dead-channel mask from per-channel variance; band-collapse -> find burst\ncsd = np.nanstd(I, axis=1)\nmed = np.nanmedian(csd[csd > 0])\nchan_ok = np.isfinite(csd) & (csd > 0.2 * med) & (csd < 8.0 * med)\nfrom scipy.signal import savgol_filter\n\ncollapse = np.nansum(np.nan_to_num(I[chan_ok]), 0)\npk = int(np.argmax(savgol_filter(collapse, 51, 3)))\nnoise = np.nanstd(collapse[: len(collapse) // 4]) + 1e-9\nsnr = (collapse[pk] - np.nanmedian(collapse)) / noise\nprint(f\"dt={dt:.3e}s ntime={I.shape[1]} chan_ok={chan_ok.sum()} burst@{pk} (t={pk*dt*1e3:.1f}ms) SNR~{snr:.1f}\")\n\n# (3) tight window around the burst, downsample channels for speed\nW = 200  # +/- samples (2.56us -> ~0.5ms window; burst is intra-channel narrow after dedisp)\nlo, hi = max(pk - W, 0), min(pk + W, I.shape[1])\ngood = np.where(chan_ok)[0][::3]\nfrg = freq[good]\nwin = np.nan_to_num(I[good][:, lo:hi])  # (nch, 2W) RAW\n\n# (4) DM-phase on a PHYSICAL residual grid around 0 (data already dedispersed at DM_C)\ngrid = np.arange(-3.0, 3.0, 0.05)\nest = DMPhaseEstimator(win.T, frg, dt, grid, ref=\"top\", n_boot=60, random_state=0)\ncurve = est.result()[\"dm_curve\"]\ni = int(np.argmax(curve))\nbs_peaks = grid[np.argmax(est._bs_curves, axis=1)]\ndm_resid = float(grid[i])\ndm_chime = DM_C + dm_resid\ndm_err = float(np.std(bs_peaks, ddof=1))\nflat = float(curve.max() / curve.min())\ninterior = bool(0 < i < len(grid) - 1)\nprint(f\"PHYSICAL grid: dm_resid={dm_resid:+.3f} dm_chime={dm_chime:.3f}±{dm_err:.3f} \"\n      f\"flat_ratio={flat:.2f} interior={interior}\")\nprint(f\"  -> {'SHARP PEAK (real structure-DM)' if flat > 3.0 else 'FLAT (no trustworthy DM)'}\")\n\n# (5) figure: waterfall + profile + DM-phase curve\nfig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.2))\nnf = (chan_ok.sum() // 4) * 4\nwf_disp = np.nan_to_num(I[chan_ok][:nf, lo:hi])\nmu = wf_disp.mean(1, keepdims=True); sd = wf_disp.std(1, keepdims=True) + 1e-9\nax[0].imshow(((wf_disp - mu) / sd).reshape(nf // 4, 4, hi - lo).mean(1), aspect=\"auto\",\n             origin=\"lower\", extent=[(lo - pk) * dt * 1e3, (hi - pk) * dt * 1e3, freq.min(), freq.max()],\n             vmin=-0.5, vmax=5, cmap=\"magma\")\nax[0].set(title=f\"zach proper-dedisp ({chan_ok.sum()} ch)\", xlabel=\"t (ms)\", ylabel=\"freq MHz\")\nax[1].plot((np.arange(hi - lo) - (pk - lo)) * dt * 1e3, collapse[lo:hi], lw=0.8, color=\"0.2\")\nax[1].set(title=f\"profile SNR~{snr:.1f}\", xlabel=\"t (ms)\")\nax[2].plot(DM_C + grid, curve, \".-\", ms=3)\nax[2].axvline(DM_C, color=\"k\", ls=\":\", label=f\"DM_c={DM_C:g}\")\nax[2].axvspan(dm_chime - dm_err, dm_chime + dm_err, color=\"r\", alpha=0.2)\nax[2].axvline(dm_chime, color=\"r\", label=f\"DM={dm_chime:.2f}±{dm_err:.2f}\")\nax[2].set(title=f\"DM-phase flat={flat:.2f} interior={interior}\", xlabel=\"trial DM\")\nax[2].legend(fontsize=8)\nfig.tight_layout()\nfig.savefig(ROOT + \"/diagnostics/proto_zach.png\", dpi=110)\nprint(\"wrote diagnostics/proto_zach.png\")\n"

> AGENT

Now I can see it clearly. Panel 1: proper dedispersion **does** recover zach's burst — a compact band-limited knot at ~400–470 MHz. But panel 3's DM-phase curve is still only weakly peaked (flat_ratio 2.13), and I spotted a likely methodological flaw in my *prototype* (not the estimator):

**The window is too tight for the residual grid.** For zach's band (~400–550 MHz), a residual ΔDM=1 produces a dispersive delay of `K_DM·1·(1/400²−1/550²) ≈ 12 ms` — but my window is only ±0.5 ms. So across the ±3 grid the burst structure shifts far outside the window, distorting/flattening the curve. The tight window was inherited from the old (1000×-too-small) recipe where delays were artificially tiny.

Let me test this decisively: sweep window width on zach **and** freya (DM 912, the best-case "real" burst) in one docker run. If a wider window sharpens the curve, the prototype just needs proper sizing; if even freya stays flat, structure-max is the wrong tool for these smooth bursts.

  "content": "\"\"\"P2 sweep: does window width control the DM-phase peak sharpness?\n\nFor zach (DM262, band-limited, low S/N) and freya (DM912, best-case 'real'):\n  proper coherent_dedisp -> find burst -> for several half-windows W, run DM-phase on a\n  PHYSICAL residual grid and report flat_ratio (peak sharpness) + recovered residual DM.\nWindow must be wide enough to contain the residual-DM sweep across the burst's band:\n  delay(ms) = K_DM*1e3 * dDM * (1/f_lo^2 - 1/f_hi^2). Report that scale per burst.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nos.environ.setdefault(\"MPLCONFIGDIR\", \"/tmp/mpl\")\nsys.path.insert(0, \"/data/research/astrophysics/frbs/chime-dsa-codetections/scripts\")\nimport matplotlib\n\nmatplotlib.use(\"Agg\")\nimport numpy as np\nfrom baseband_analysis.core.bbdata import BBData\nfrom baseband_analysis.core.dedispersion import coherent_dedisp\nfrom dmphase_standalone import K_DM, DMPhaseEstimator\nfrom scipy.signal import savgol_filter\n\nROOT = \"/data/research/astrophysics/frbs/chime-dsa-codetections\"\nCASES = [(\"zach\", \"210456524\", 262.368), (\"freya\", \"278720455\", 912.4)]\n\n\ndef run(name, cid, dm_c):\n    bb = BBData.from_file(f\"{ROOT}/chime_singlebeam/singlebeam_{cid}.h5\")\n    dt = float(bb.attrs[\"delta_time\"])\n    freq = np.asarray(bb.index_map[\"freq\"][\"centre\"], float)\n    bbdd = coherent_dedisp(bb, dm_c)\n    I = np.abs(bbdd[:, 0, :]) ** 2 + np.abs(bbdd[:, 1, :]) ** 2\n    csd = np.nanstd(I, axis=1)\n    med = np.nanmedian(csd[csd > 0])\n    chan_ok = np.isfinite(csd) & (csd > 0.2 * med) & (csd < 8.0 * med)\n    collapse = np.nansum(np.nan_to_num(I[chan_ok]), 0)\n    pk = int(np.argmax(savgol_filter(collapse, 51, 3)))\n    # band where signal actually lives (channels whose peak-region power is high)\n    chs = np.where(chan_ok)[0]\n    flo, fhi = freq[chs].min(), freq[chs].max()\n    delay_per_dm_ms = K_DM * 1e3 * (1.0 / flo**2 - 1}\")\n\n\nfor c in CASES:\n    run(*c)\n"

Still running after 9+ min — I over-sized it. The W=5000 cases are computationally explosive: DM-phase is O(n_grid × n_t × n_ch × n_boot), and at dt=2.56µs a ±12.8ms window is 10000 time samples — these bursts are ms-scale, so that's ~1000× oversampled. Killing it and fixing the real engineering issue: **time-downsample before DM-phase** (2.56µs → ~0.2ms keeps ms structure, slashes n_t), which makes wide windows cheap.

  "new_string": "    good = chs[::3]\n    frg = freq[good]\n    # time-downsample to ~ms resolution: DM-phase wants ms structure, 2.56us is ~1000x oversampled.\n    # Window expressed in MILLISECONDS (physical), converted to samples per burst.\n    grid = np.arange(-1.5, 1.5, 0.03)  # narrow: data already dedispersed at DM_c, residual is small\n    for win_ms, tds in ((4.0, 8), (12.0, 16), (30.0, 32)):\n        Wd = int(win_ms / (dt * 1e3))  # half-window in raw samples\n        lo, hi = max(pk - Wd, 0), min(pk + Wd, I.shape[1])\n        seg = np.nan_to_num(I[good][:, lo:hi])\n        nt = (seg.shape[1] // tds) * tds\n        segd = seg[:, :nt].reshape(seg.shape[0], nt // tds, tds).mean(2)  # downsample in time\n        dt_ds = dt * tds\n        est = DMPhaseEstimator(segd.T, frg, dt_ds, grid, ref=\"top\", n_boot=40, random_state=0)\n        c = est.result()[\"dm_curve\"]\n        i = int(np.argmax(c))\n        flat = c.max() / c.min()\n        print(\n            f\"   win=±{win_ms:5.1f}ms tds={tds:3d} (dt_ds={dt_ds * 1e3:.2f}ms, nt={nt // tds:4d})  \"\n            f\"flat_ratio={flat:5.2f}  dm_resid={grid[i]:+.2f}  dm={dm_c + grid[i]:.2f}  \"\n            f\"interior={0 < i < len(grid) - 1}\"\n        )"

This is a methodology question, not a coding task — no files to touch. Let me give you the rigorous call.

Short version: your instinct is correct on every major point. flat_ratio ~2 is a non-detection of structure, structure-max DM is the wrong tool here, and the residual-near-zero is circular as currently framed. Below is the full reasoning, the metrics/thresholds, and the recommended path.

## 1. Is flat_ratio ~2 a non-detection? Yes.

Structure-maximizing DM (DM_phase; Seymour, Michilli, Hessels et al. 2019; conceptual roots in Gajjar+2018 / Hessels+2019 "DM_struct") maximizes a *coherence/sharpness* functional of the dedispersed dynamic spectrum as a function of trial DM. The functional has curvature in DM **only to the extent that there is unresolved temporal structure that incorrect DM smears**. The width of the peak scales like the structure timescale: a feature of width δt across bandwidth B around ν gives a DM curvature whose FWHM in DM is roughly

ΔDM_FWHM ≈ δt / [k_DM · (ν_lo⁻² − ν_hi⁻²)],  k_DM ≈ 4.149 ms·GHz²·(pc/cm³)⁻¹

So the **sharpness of the curve is set by the sharpness of the burst, not by how correct your DM is**. Your synthetic case (2-ms-separated sub-pulses, full band) has exactly the kind of sub-structure the metric is built to exploit → flat_ratio 48.5. A single scattered/intrinsically-broad blob has no such feature → the metric is flat by construction.

Critically: **a flat curve is fully consistent with a perfectly correct DM.** flat_ratio ~2 does *not* mean "DM wrong"; it means "no exploitable micro-structure." That is exactly your interpretation, and it is right. The near-invariance under window width (±4 → ±12 ms) is corroborating: a real structure peak would not change with window; a noise-dominated metric wanders slightly as you admit more noise/baseline, which is the +0.09 → +0.78 drift you see. That drift is the metric chasing noise, not refining a DM.

**Gate for a real structure-DM detection.** flat_ratio (max/min) is a poor statistic because its null depends on window length, channelization, and noise realization. Don't gate on a fixed flat_ratio number. Gate on **significance of the peak against a null built from the same data**:

- Build the null by either (i) phase-scrambling each channel (destroys temporal structure, preserves noise/bandpass) or (ii) running the identical estimator on off-pulse data with the same window. Compute the structure metric distribution under the null.
- Detection significance = (peak_metric − median_null) / MAD_null, i.e. an effective S/N of the *peak*, not the curve.
- Require ≳ 5σ against that null **and** a peak whose ΔDM_FWHM is finite and smaller than your DM search span (a peak that fills the search window is not a peak).
- Sanity floor: flat_ratio of a genuine detection on real data is typically ≳ 5–10; your ~2 is below any reasonable floor. But report the null-based significance, not flat_ratio, as the gate.

For zach: ~2, window-dependent, no localized peak → **null**. Correct call.

## 2. Science goal is "do the DMs agree" → use S/N-maximizing DM. Yes, switch.

For "does CHIME's DM agree with DSA's," you do **not** need structure; you need the best band-integrated DM with an honest error bar. That is **S/N-maximizing DM** (the standard CHIME/FRB pipeline convention; Petroff, Hessels & Lorimer 2019 review; CHIME/FRB Catalog 1, Amiri et al. 2021 — fitburst). It maximizes the peak (or integrated) S/N of the frequency-collapsed, dedispersed profile and works on smooth bursts precisely because it doesn't require sub-structure.

**The scattering bias is real and must be handled, not ignored.** S/N-DM on a one-sided scatter-broadened pulse biases the DM because the estimator can trade dispersive tilt against the scattering tail — it tends to push the DM so the sharp leading edge aligns, and the magnitude/sign depends on how you define the S/N (peak vs. integrated) and on the pulse shape. The fix is the one CHIME/FRB and the pulsar community use:

- **Fit a forward model**, not a bare S/N maximizer: a dispersed pulse = intrinsic profile ⊗ scattering kernel (one-sided exponential ∝ exp(−t/τ), τ ∝ ν⁻⁴) ⊗ intra-channel dispersive smearing, with DM, scattering τ, amplitude, t0, and (per-band) spectral index as free parameters. **You already have this** — `burstfit.py` (FRBModel/FRBFitter, models M0–M3) is exactly a DM + scattering forward model. M3 fits `delta_dm` and `tau_1ghz` jointly. Use it. Fitting τ simultaneously with DM is what removes the scattering–DM covariance; a bare S/N-max does not.
- This is strictly better than S/N-max for your data: same applicability to smooth bursts, but it *models* the tail instead of being fooled by it, and it gives you a posterior on DM marginalized over τ.

So the practical estimator is not "S/N-max vs structure-max" — it's **forward-model the CHIME burst with burstfit M2/M3 and read off the marginalized DM posterior**, with `delta_dm` referenced to whatever DM you coherently dedispersed at.

**Uncertainty.** Three contributions, combine in quadrature:
- **Statistical:** the marginalized posterior width on `delta_dm` from the fit (MCMC in burstfit). At band-collapse S/N 3–11 this will be the dominant, and honestly large, term — that's fine, it's the truth.
- **Scattering systematic:** the DM shift between a fit with τ free and τ fixed to 0 (or to a prior), i.e. how much the DM moves when you let the tail absorb structure. Report it.
- **Reference/band systematic:** intra-channel smearing and the finite 400 MHz CHIME band. Run the validation gates in the repo (`VALIDATION_THRESHOLDS`); the τ×Δν ∈ [0.1, 2.0] and α physical-bounds checks are exactly the right guards.

Report DM_CHIME = DM_dedisp + δ̂_DM ± (σ_stat ⊕ σ_scat). Expect σ of order a few pc/cm³ for the smooth low-S/N bursts — and that is the scientifically honest answer.

## 3. Circularity — your sharpest worry, and it's valid.

You coherently dedispersed at the DSA DM, then measured a residual ≈ 0. **As stated, that is partially circular and weakly informative**, for two reasons:

1. Coherent dedispersion at DM_DSA does not pin the *measured* DM — a residual fit can still recover an offset (your synthetic recovered DM=20 exactly after dedispersing at 20, with δ=0, and a wrong injected DM would have shown δ≠0). So the *estimator* is unbiased w.r.t. the reference. **But** the prior/window is centered on DM_DSA, and at low S/N the likelihood is broad, so the posterior is pulled toward the reference by construction. A residual consistent with zero at σ≫0 is the expected outcome whether or not the DMs truly agree to high precision.
2. The actual test you can defend is **not** "δ_DM = 0." It is: **"an independent CHIME DM measurement has a posterior that overlaps DM_DSA, and the CHIME data are inconsistent with a DM far from DM_DSA at some confidence."** That's an *exclusion* statement, and it's only meaningful if your DM search/prior is wide enough that a disagreeing DM *could* have been found.

**How to de-circularize, concretely:**
- **Search wide, independent of the reference.** Run the DM estimator (forward-fit or S/N-max) over a broad DM grid — e.g. DM_DSA ± several × your expected σ, at minimum ±20–50 pc/cm³, ideally a flat prior spanning it — *not* a tight ±4 ms window centered on the reference. Let the data choose. Report the marginalized DM posterior over that wide range.
- **Pre-register the agreement metric.** Define agreement *before* looking: e.g. |DM_CHIME − DM_DSA| / σ_CHIME < 2 (or a Bayesian: posterior odds that |Δ| < tolerance). State the tolerance from physics — the two telescopes see different ν, so even a *true* common DM can differ by the frequency-dependent scattering/profile-evolution and intra-channel terms; a few pc/cm³ tolerance is physical.
- **Report the constraint, not just the point.** "CHIME DM = X ± σ; consistent with DSA DM = Y; CHIME data exclude |ΔDM| > Z at 95%." If σ_CHIME is so large that Z is bigger than any astrophysically interesting offset, then **the honest statement is that CHIME singlebeam does not independently constrain the DM** — which is path (d) for that burst, and that's a legitimate, publishable outcome.
- **Avoid the trap of quoting δ≈0 from a reference-centered narrow window as evidence.** That number is mostly an artifact of the window. The wide-search posterior is the only non-circular product.

## 4. Recommended path

**(c) restricted to a forward-fit core, with (d) as the per-burst fallback.** Concretely:

1. **Drop structure-max as the primary estimator.** Keep it only as a *secondary cross-check*, reported with the null-based significance gate from §1. For most of your 12 (smooth, low-S/N) it will null — report that honestly; it is not a failure, it's the correct statement that there's no micro-structure to exploit. Do **not** report structure-max DMs that come from flat curves.

2. **Primary CHIME DM = burstfit forward-model fit (M2/M3) over a wide, reference-independent DM prior**, marginalized DM posterior, τ fitted simultaneously to absorb scattering bias. This is your defensible, scattering-aware, smooth-burst-capable estimator, and it's already in the repo. Run the mandatory PASS/MARGINAL/FAIL validation gates on every fit.

3. **Per burst, classify the outcome:**
   - **Constrains DM:** posterior σ small enough that the agreement test (pre-registered, §3) is decisive → report DM_CHIME ± σ and the |Δ| exclusion. These bursts support Pillar-2.
   - **Does not constrain DM:** posterior σ too broad (the expected case for several S/N~3 blobs) → state "CHIME singlebeam does not independently confirm DM for this burst" and lean on positional/temporal pillars. This is path (d), applied selectively, not globally.

4. **Don't suspend Pillar-2 wholesale (full (d)) and don't oversell it.** The right framing for the paper is: "For the N bursts with sufficient CHIME S/N, an independent scattering-aware DM fit agrees with DSA within errors and excludes ΔDM > Z; for the remaining bursts CHIME singlebeam S/N is too low to independently constrain DM, and association rests on position + time." That is both rigorous and stronger than a blanket structure-max table full of flat curves.

### Metric/threshold summary
- **Structure-DM gate (cross-check only):** null-based peak significance ≥ 5σ (phase-scramble or off-pulse null), localized peak with finite ΔDM_FWHM < search span. flat_ratio ~2 → null. (Your zach: null — correct.)
- **Primary estimator:** burstfit M2/M3, τ free, wide reference-independent DM prior; report marginalized DM posterior.
- **Uncertainty:** σ_stat (posterior) ⊕ σ_scat (DM shift τ-free vs τ-fixed); guard with τ×Δν ∈ [0.1,2.0], α ∈ [1.5,6.0] (repo gates).
- **Agreement test (pre-registered):** |DM_CHIME − DM_DSA|/σ_CHIME < 2, plus a stated |ΔDM| exclusion at 95%; physical tolerance of a few pc/cm³ for cross-telescope offsets.
- **De-circularize:** wide independent DM search; report the exclusion, not the reference-centered δ≈0.

### Key methodology anchors
- DM_phase / structure-max: Seymour, Michilli & Hessels (DM_phase); Hessels et al. 2019; Gajjar et al. 2018 — structure metric requires unresolved sub-structure.
- S/N-DM convention + fitburst forward modeling: CHIME/FRB Catalog 1 (Amiri et al. 2021); Petroff, Hessels & Lorimer 2019 (review).
- Scattering–DM covariance and τ ∝ ν⁻⁴ kernel: standard pulse-broadening treatment; handled in your `burstfit.py` M2/M3.

One caveat to flag for yourself: confirm what DM the CHIME baseband was *recorded/coherently* dedispersed at versus what you re-dedispersed at — `delta_dm` is only interpretable relative to a known reference DM, and intra-channel coherent dedispersion at the wrong DM is not undone by an incoherent re-trial. If the coherent step used DM_DSA, your residual fit is incoherent-only and that's fine; just state it.

> AGENT

Now building the tool. The method is the **textbook-rigorous DM measurement**, not structure-max: split the band into sub-bands, fit a scatter-corrected arrival time in each (exponentially-modified Gaussian → the intrinsic `t0`, deconvolved from the scattering tail), then weighted-linear-regress arrival time vs ν⁻². The slope *is* the DM residual; the regression gives an honest σ_DM and degrades gracefully to "doesn't constrain" at low S/N. Pure numpy/scipy, no flits deps.

{
  "file_path": "/home/ubuntu/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/dispersion/chime_dm.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Custom CHIME DM measurement: scatter-corrected arrival-time regression over a wide prior.\n\nPurpose-built to replace the structure-maximizing ``DMPhaseEstimator`` for CHIME singlebeam\nbursts, which are smooth / scatter-broadened / low-S/N and lack the temporal sub-structure that\nstructure-max needs (see .agents/audit-chime-side-dm.md; expert methodology verdict 2026-06-24).\n\nMethod (the textbook DM measurement, scattering-aware):\n  given an intensity waterfall already coherently dedispersed at ``dm_ref``,\n  1. split the band into sub-bands; in each, band-collapse to a profile and fit an\n     exponentially-modified Gaussian (intrinsic Gaussian (x) one-sided scattering exp(-t/tau)).\n     The fitted Gaussian centre ``t0`` is the scattering-DECONVOLVED arrival time (so the\n     scattering tail does not bias it, unlike a peak/centroid S/N-DM);\n  2. weighted-linear-regress t0_i against x_i = K_DM*(nu_i^-2 - nu_ref^-2). The slope is the\n     residual DM (DM - dm_ref); the regression covariance gives an honest sigma_DM.\n  Smooth low-S/N bursts -> few sub-bands survive / noisy t0 -> large sigma_DM, flagged as\n  \"does not constrain DM\" rather than a fabricated value.\n\nPure numpy/scipy (no flits imports) so the SAME module runs in the baseband docker image and on\nthe host. K_DM mirrors flits.common.constants.K_DM.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom scipy.optimize import curve_fit\nfrom scipy.special import erfcx\n\nK_DM = 4.148808e3  # s MHz^2 pc^-1 cm^3 (== flits.common.constants.K_DM; inlined for docker)\n\n\ndef exgauss(t, t0, sigma, tau, amp, base):\n    \"\"\"Exponentially-modified Gaussian (Gaussian(sigma) convolved one-sided exp(-t/tau)).\n\n    Stable form via erfcx (erfcx(z) = exp(z^2) erfc(z)) so the exp never overflows. ``t0`` is\n    the centre of the intrinsic Gaussian = the scattering-deconvolved arrival time.\n    \"\"\"\n    sigma = abs(sigma) + 1e-12\n    tau = abs(tau) + 1e-12\n    dt = t - t0\n    z = (sigma / tau - dt / sigma) / np.sqrt(2.0)\n    return base + amp * np.exp(-0.5 * (dt / sigma) ** 2) * erfcx(z)\n\n\ndef _fit_subband_arrival(profile, dt, min_snr=4.0):\n    \"\"\"Fit a scattered pulse to a 1-D profile; return (t0_s, t0_err_s, snr) or None.\n\n    t0 is the intrinsic (scattering-corrected) arrival time in seconds from the window start.\n    \"\"\"\n    n = profile.size\n    t = np.arange(n) * dt\n    base0 = float(np.median(profile))\n    off = profile[: max(n // 5, 5)]\n    noise = float(np.std(off)) + 1e-12\n    pk = int(np.argmax(profile))\n    amp0 = float(profile[pk] - base0)\n    snr0 = amp0 / noise\n    if snr0 < min_snr:\n        return None\n    # rough width: samples above half-max around the peak\n    half = base0 + 0.5 * amp0\n    above = np.where(profile > half)[0]\n    w0 = max((above.max() - above.min()) * dt, 2 * dt) if above.size > 1 else 4 * dt\n    p0 = [t[pk] - 0.3 * w0, 0.4 * w0, 0.4 * w0, amp0, base0]  # t0 slightly before peak (scatter)\n    bounds = (\n        [0.0, dt, 0.0, 0.2 * amp0, base0 - 5 * noise],\n        [t[-1], n * dt, n * dt, 5 * amp0, base0 + 5 * noise],\n    )\n    try:\n        popt, pcov = curve_fit(\n            exgauss, t, profile, p0=p0, bounds=bounds, sigma=np.full(n, noise), maxfev=6000\n        )\n    except (RuntimeError, ValueError):\n        return None\n    t0, sigma, tau, amp, base = popt\n    t0_err = float(np.sqrt(abs(pcov[0, 0])))\n    if not np.isfinite(t0_err) or t0_err <= 0:\n        return None\n    snr = amp / noise\n    if snr < min_snr or t0_err > 0.5 * n * dt:  # unconstrained arrival -> reject\n        return None\n    return float(t0), t0_err, float(snr)\n\n\ndef measure_dm(\n    wf,\n    freqs,\n    dt,\n    dm_ref,\n    n_subband=8,\n    min_snr=4.0,\n    min_good_subbands=3,\n    dm_err_max=15.0,\n):\n    \"\"\"Measure DM from a coherently-dedispersed (at ``dm_ref``) intensity waterfall.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    wf : (n_freq, n_time) array — intensity, frequency axis matching ``freqs``.\n    freqs : (n_freq,) channel centre frequencies [MHz] (any order).\n    dt : float — time resolution [s].\n    dm_ref : float — DM the data was coherently dedispersed at [pc/cm^3].\n\n    Returns a dict with dm, dm_err (None if unconstrained), constrains_dm (bool), reason,\n    n_good_subbands, snr, tau_ms, and the per-subband (freq, t0, t0_err, snr) for diagnostics.\n    \"\"\"\n    wf = np.asarray(wf, float)\n    freqs = np.asarray(freqs, float)\n    order = np.argsort(freqs)  # ascending\n    wf, freqs = wf[order], freqs[order]\n    nu_ref = freqs.max()\n\n    edges = np.linspace(0, wf.shape[0], n_subband + 1, dtype=int)\n    sub_nu, sub_t0, sub_err, sub_snr = [], [], [], []\n    for a, b in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]):\n        if b - a < 1:\n            continue\n        prof = np.nansum(np.nan_to_num(wf[a:b]), axis=0)\n        fit = _fit_subband_arrival(prof, dt, min_snr=min_snr)\n        if fit is None:\n            continue\n        t0, t0_err, snr = fit\n        sub_nu.append(float(freqs[a:b].mean()))\n        sub_t0.append(t0)\n        sub_err.append(t0_err)\n        sub_snr.append(snr)\n\n    n_good = len(sub_nu)\n    overall_snr = float(np.sqrt(np.sum(np.square(sub_snr)))) if sub_snr else 0.0\n    base = {\n        \"dm_ref\": float(dm_ref),\n        \"n_good_subbands\": n_good,\n        \"snr\": overall_snr,\n        \"subbands\": [\n            {\"freq_mhz\": f, \"t0_s\": t, \"t0_err_s\": e, \"snr\": s}\n            for f, t, e, s in zip(sub_nu, sub_t0, sub_err, sub_snr)\n        ],\n    }\n    if n_good < min_good_subbands:\n        return {\n            **base, \"dm\": None, \"dm_err\": None, \"tau_ms\": None, \"constrains_dm\": False,\n            \"reason\": f\"only {n_good} sub-bands above S/N {min_snr} (<{min_good_subbands})\",\n        }\n\n    nu = np.array(sub_nu)\n    t0 = np.array(sub_t0)\n    err = np.array(sub_err)\n    x = K_DM * (1.0 / nu**2 - 1.0 / nu_ref**2)  # s per unit residual DM\n    # weighted linear fit t0 = slope*x + c ; slope = residual DM\n    w = 1.0 / err**2\n    X = np.vstack([x, np.ones_like(x)]).T\n    WX = X * w[:, None]\n    cov = np.linalg.inv(X.T @ WX)\n    beta = cov @ (WX.T @ t0)\n    slope, _ = beta\n    slope_err = float(np.sqrt(abs(cov[0, 0])))\n    dm = float(dm_ref + slope)\n    dm_err = slope_err\n    constrains = bool(np.isfinite(dm_err) and dm_err < dm_err_max)\n    return {\n        **base,\n        \"dm\": dm,\n        \"dm_err\": dm_err,\n        \"tau_ms\": None,\n        \"constrains_dm\": constrains,\n        \"reason\": \"ok\" if constrains else f\"sigma_DM={dm_err:.1f} >= {dm_err_max} pc/cm^3\",\n    }\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/home/ubuntu/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/tests/test_chime_dm.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Validate the custom CHIME DM tool (dispersion/chime_dm.py) on synthetic known-truth bursts.\n\nThe injector is INDEPENDENT of the estimator: it builds each channel profile by numerically\nconvolving an intrinsic Gaussian with a one-sided scattering exponential (not the module's\nerfcx exgauss), then disperses channels by the residual DM. So a pass means the tool recovers a\nknown DM from a realistic scattered, dispersed, noisy waterfall — not that it agrees with itself.\n\nCovers the regime that broke structure-max: smooth pulses (no sub-structure), scattering tails,\nlow S/N, and a non-detection floor.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pytest\n\nfrom dispersion.chime_dm import K_DM, measure_dm\n\n\ndef _inject(freqs, dt, n_t, dm_ref, dm_true, t0_base, sigma_ms, tau_ref_ms, snr, rng):\n    \"\"\"Waterfall (n_freq, n_t) of a scattered pulse dispersed by (dm_true - dm_ref).\n\n    Per channel: Gaussian(sigma_ms) (x) exp(-t/tau(nu)), tau(nu)=tau_ref*(nu/nu_ref)^-4,\n    centred at the residual-dispersion arrival time. White noise scaled to the target per-channel\n    peak S/N (band-collapsed S/N is ~sqrt(n_freq) higher).\n    \"\"\"\n    nu_ref = freqs.max()\n    t = np.arange(n_t) * dt\n    wf = np.zeros((freqs.size, n_t))\n    ddm = dm_true - dm_ref\n    sig = sigma_ms * 1e-3\n    for j, nu in enumerate(freqs):\n        arr = t0_base + ddm * K_DM * (1.0 / nu**2 - 1.0 / nu_ref**2)\n        g = np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - arr) / sig) ** 2)\n        tau = tau_ref_ms * 1e-3 * (nu / nu_ref) ** -4\n        if tau > 1e-6:\n            k = np.exp(-np.arange(0, 8 * tau, dt) / tau)\n            g = np.convolve(g, k, mode=\"full\")[: n_t]\n        g /= g.max() + 1e-12\n        wf[j] = snr * g + rng.standard_normal(n_t)\n    return wf\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"dm_true_off,tau_ref_ms\",\n    [(5.0, 0.0), (-8.0, 0.0), (30.0, 0.0), (12.0, 2.0), (-15.0, 5.0)],\n)\ndef test_recovers_known_dm(dm_true_off, tau_ref_ms):\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)\n    freqs = np.linspace(400.0, 800.0, 96)\n    dt, n_t, dm_ref = 1.0e-3, 1400, 500.0\n    dm_true = dm_ref + dm_true_off\n    wf = _inject(freqs, dt, n_t, dm_ref, dm_true, 0.6, 1.5, tau_ref_ms, snr=4.0, rng=rng)\n\n    res = measure_dm(wf, freqs, dt, dm_ref)\n    assert res[\"constrains_dm\"], f\"should constrain DM: {res['reason']} (n={res['n_good_subbands']})\"\n    # recovered within max(3 sigma, 2 pc/cm^3) of truth, and sigma is honest (not over-confident)\n    assert abs(res[\"dm\"] - dm_true) < max(3.0 * res[\"dm_err\"], 2.0), (\n        f\"dm={res['dm']:.2f} truth={dm_true} sigma={res['dm_err']:.2f}\"\n    )\n\n\ndef test_flags_nondetection_at_low_snr():\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)\n    freqs = np.linspace(400.0, 800.0, 96)\n    dt, n_t, dm_ref = 1.0e-3, 1400, 500.0\n    # per-channel S/N ~1: no sub-band should clear the S/N floor -> not constrained, not fabricated\n    wf = _inject(freqs, dt, n_t, dm_ref, dm_ref + 10.0, 0.6, 1.5, 0.0, snr=0.8, rng=rng)\n    res = measure_dm(wf, freqs, dt, dm_ref)\n    assert not res[\"constrains_dm\"]\n    assert res[\"dm\"] is None or res[\"dm_err\"] is None\n\n\ndef test_sigma_is_calibrated_across_realizations():\n    # over many noise realizations the pull (dm-truth)/sigma should be ~unit-scatter, not >>1\n    freqs = np.linspace(400.0, 800.0, 96)\n    dt, n_t, dm_ref = 1.0e-3, 1400, 500.0\n    dm_true = dm_ref + 10.0\n    pulls = []\n    for s in range(12):\n        rng = np.random.default_rng(100 + s)\n        wf = _inject(freqs, dt, n_t, dm_ref, dm_true, 0.6, 1.5, 1.0, snr=5.0, rng=rng)\n        res = measure_dm(wf, freqs, dt, dm_ref)\n        if res[\"constrains_dm\"]:\n            pulls.append((res[\"dm\"] - dm_true) / res[\"dm_err\"])\n    assert len(pulls) >= 8, f\"too few constrained fits ({len(pulls)}/12)\"\n    assert np.std(pulls) < 3.0, f\"pull scatter {np.std(pulls):.2f} — sigma is over-confident\"\n"
}

> AGENT

The synthetic test caught a real design flaw immediately — exactly what test-first is for. The tool assumed the residual DM is tiny (data already at `dm_ref`), so large residuals smear the pulse *within* each sub-band and kill the per-band S/N. That also blocks the wide reference-independent search the expert requires (to *exclude* large offsets, the tool must be able to detect them). 

Fix: add a **coarse incoherent dedispersion search** (stage 1) to lock the DM over a wide grid, then the scatter-corrected arrival-time regression (stage 2) at that DM for the precise value + honest σ. This also makes it work on DSA's narrow band. Rewriting:

{
  "file_path": "/home/ubuntu/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/dispersion/chime_dm.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Telescope-agnostic DM measurement: wide incoherent search + scatter-corrected arrival regression.\n\nPurpose-built to replace the structure-maximizing ``DMPhaseEstimator`` for co-detection bursts that\nare smooth / scatter-broadened / low-S/N and lack the temporal sub-structure structure-max needs\n(see .agents/audit-chime-side-dm.md; expert methodology verdict 2026-06-24). Works on any band given\na ``freqs`` array — validated on both CHIME (400-800 MHz) and DSA-110 (~1.28-1.53 GHz) regimes.\n\nTwo stages, on an intensity waterfall already coherently dedispersed at ``dm_ref``:\n  STAGE 1 (wide, reference-independent): incoherently re-dedisperse over a broad trial-DM grid and\n    take the band-collapsed peak S/N -> a coarse DM that can be far from dm_ref (so a real offset\n    CAN be found -> the agreement test is an exclusion, not a circular delta~0).\n  STAGE 2 (precise, scattering-aware): at the coarse DM, split the band into sub-bands, fit each\n    band-collapsed profile with an exponentially-modified Gaussian (Gaussian (x) one-sided\n    exp(-t/tau)); the fitted Gaussian centre t0 is the scattering-DECONVOLVED arrival time.\n    Weighted-linear-regress t0 vs K_DM*(nu^-2 - nu_ref^-2): slope = residual DM, covariance = sigma_DM.\n  Smooth low-S/N bursts -> few sub-bands survive / large sigma_DM -> \"does not constrain DM\" (no\n  fabricated value), leaning on other association pillars.\n\nPure numpy/scipy (no flits imports) so the SAME module runs in the baseband docker image and host.\nK_DM mirrors flits.common.constants.K_DM.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom scipy.optimize import curve_fit\nfrom scipy.special import erfcx\n\nK_DM = 4.148808e3  # s MHz^2 pc^-1 cm^3 (== flits.common.constants.K_DM; inlined for docker)\n\n\ndef exgauss(t, t0, sigma, tau, amp, base):\n    \"\"\"Exponentially-modified Gaussian (Gaussian(sigma) convolved one-sided exp(-t/tau)).\n\n    Stable via erfcx (erfcx(z)=exp(z^2)erfc(z)) so the exp never overflows. ``t0`` is the centre of\n    the intrinsic Gaussian = the scattering-deconvolved arrival time.\n    \"\"\"\n    sigma = abs(sigma) + 1e-12\n    tau = abs(tau) + 1e-12\n    dt = t - t0\n    z = (sigma / tau - dt / sigma) / np.sqrt(2.0)\n    return base + amp * np.exp(-0.5 * (dt / sigma) ** 2) * erfcx(z)\n\n\ndef _dedisperse(wf, freqs, dt, ddm, nu_ref):\n    \"\"\"Incoherently shift each channel by the dispersive delay of a residual DM ``ddm``.\"\"\"\n    shifts = np.round(K_DM * ddm * (1.0 / freqs**2 - 1.0 / nu_ref**2) / dt).astype(int)\n    return np.array([np.roll(wf[j], -shifts[j]) for j in range(freqs.size)])\n\n\ndef _coarse_dm(wf, freqs, dt, nu_ref, dm_window, dm_step):\n    \"\"\"Stage 1: band-collapsed peak S/N over a wide residual-DM grid. Returns (ddm*, grid, snr, i).\"\"\"\n    grid = np.arange(-dm_window, dm_window + dm_step, dm_step)\n    snr = np.empty(grid.size)\n    for k, ddm in enumerate(grid):\n        prof = _dedisperse(wf, freqs, dt, ddm, nu_ref).sum(0)\n        noise = np.std(prof[: max(prof.size // 5, 5)]) + 1e-12\n        snr[k] = (prof.max() - np.median(prof)) / noise\n    i = int(np.argmax(snr))\n    return float(grid[i]), grid, snr, i\n\n\ndef _fit_subband_arrival(profile, dt, min_snr=4.0):\n    \"\"\"Fit a scattered pulse to a 1-D profile; return (t0_s, t0_err_s, snr) or None.\"\"\"\n    n = profile.size\n    t = np.arange(n) * dt\n    base0 = float(np.median(profile))\n    noise = float(np.std(profile[: max(n // 5, 5)])) + 1e-12\n    pk = int(np.argmax(profile))\n    amp0 = float(profile[pk] - base0)\n    if amp0 / noise < min_snr:\n        return None\n    half = base0 + 0.5 * amp0\n    above = np.where(profile > half)[0]\n    w0 = max((above.max() - above.min()) * dt, 2 * dt) if above.size > 1 else 4 * dt\n    p0 = [t[pk] - 0.3 * w0, 0.4 * w0, 0.4 * w0, amp0, base0]\n    bounds = (\n        [0.0, dt, 0.0, 0.2 * amp0, base0 - 5 * noise],\n        [t[-1], n * dt, n * dt, 5 * amp0, base0 + 5 * noise],\n    )\n    try:\n        popt, pcov = curve_fit(\n            exgauss, t, profile, p0=p0, bounds=bounds, sigma=np.full(n, noise), maxfev=6000\n        )\n    except (RuntimeError, ValueError):\n        return None\n    t0, _sigma, _tau, amp, _base = popt\n    t0_err = float(np.sqrt(abs(pcov[0, 0])))\n    if not np.isfinite(t0_err) or t0_err <= 0 or amp / noise < min_snr or t0_err > 0.5 * n * dt:\n        return None\n    return float(t0), t0_err, float(amp / noise)\n\n\ndef measure_dm(\n    wf,\n    freqs,\n    dt,\n    dm_ref,\n    n_subband=8,\n    dm_window=50.0,\n    dm_step=0.5,\n    min_snr=4.0,\n    min_good_subbands=3,\n    dm_err_max=20.0,\n):\n    \"\"\"Measure DM from a coherently-dedispersed (at ``dm_ref``) intensity waterfall (n_freq, n_time).\n\n    ``freqs`` are channel centres [MHz] (any order); ``dt`` is [s]; ``dm_ref`` is [pc/cm^3].\n    Returns a dict: dm, dm_err (None if unconstrained), constrains_dm, reason, coarse_dm,\n    n_good_subbands, snr, plus per-subband (freq, t0, t0_err, snr) and the coarse S/N(DM) curve.\n    \"\"\"\n    wf = np.asarray(wf, float)\n    freqs = np.asarray(freqs, float)\n    order = np.argsort(freqs)\n    wf, freqs = wf[order], freqs[order]\n    nu_ref = float(freqs.max())\n\n    ddm_c, grid, snr_curve, ic = _coarse_dm(wf, freqs, dt, nu_ref, dm_window, dm_step)\n    coarse_dm = float(dm_ref + ddm_c)\n    peak_snr = float(snr_curve[ic])\n    wf_dd = _dedisperse(wf, freqs, dt, ddm_c, nu_ref)  # align at coarse DM -> small residual\n\n    edges = np.linspace(0, wf_dd.shape[0], n_subband + 1, dtype=int)\n    sub_nu, sub_t0, sub_err, sub_snr = [], [], [], []\n    for a, b in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]):\n        if b - a < 1:\n            continue\n        fit = _fit_subband_arrival(np.nansum(np.nan_to_num(wf_dd[a:b]), axis=0), dt, min_snr=min_snr)\n        if fit is None:\n            continue\n        sub_nu.append(float(freqs[a:b].mean()))\n        sub_t0.append(fit[0])\n        sub_err.append(fit[1])\n        sub_snr.append(fit[2])\n\n    n_good = len(sub_nu)\n    base = {\n        \"dm_ref\": float(dm_ref),\n        \"coarse_dm\": coarse_dm,\n        \"peak_snr\": peak_snr,\n        \"n_good_subbands\": n_good,\n        \"snr\": float(np.sqrt(np.sum(np.square(sub_snr)))) if sub_snr else 0.0,\n        \"subbands\": [\n            {\"freq_mhz\": f, \"t0_s\": t, \"t0_err_s\": e, \"snr\": s}\n            for f, t, e, s in zip(sub_nu, sub_t0, sub_err, sub_snr)\n        ],\n        \"coarse_curve\": {\"dm\": (dm_ref + grid).tolist(), \"snr\": snr_curve.tolist()},\n        \"railed\": bool(ic == 0 or ic == grid.size - 1),\n    }\n    if n_good < min_good_subbands:\n        return {\n            **base, \"dm\": None, \"dm_err\": None, \"constrains_dm\": False,\n            \"reason\": f\"only {n_good} sub-bands above S/N {min_snr} (<{min_good_subbands})\",\n        }\n\n    nu = np.array(sub_nu)\n    x = K_DM * (1.0 / nu**2 - 1.0 / nu_ref**2)  # s per unit residual DM\n    w = 1.0 / np.array(sub_err) ** 2\n    X = np.vstack([x, np.ones_like(x)]).T\n    cov = np.linalg.inv(X.T @ (X * w[:, None]))\n    slope, _c = cov @ ((X * w[:, None]).T @ np.array(sub_t0))\n    dm_err = float(np.sqrt(abs(cov[0, 0])))\n    dm = float(coarse_dm + slope)\n    constrains = bool(np.isfinite(dm_err) and dm_err < dm_err_max and not base[\"railed\"])\n    reason = \"ok\"\n    if base[\"railed\"]:\n        reason = \"coarse DM railed at search-grid edge\"\n    elif not constrains:\n        reason = f\"sigma_DM={dm_err:.1f} >= {dm_err_max} pc/cm^3\"\n    return {**base, \"dm\": dm, \"dm_err\": dm_err, \"constrains_dm\": constrains, \"reason\": reason}\n"
}

> AGENT

The `erfcx` overflow warning is the smoking gun: `erfcx(z)` is only stable for `z ≥ 0`; in the scattering tail `z` goes very negative and `erfcx` overflows to `inf`, so *every* sub-band fit throws and returns `None` → 0 good sub-bands. Need the standard piecewise-stable exGaussian (erfcx form for `z≥0`, direct `exp·erfc` for `z<0`).

  "new_string": "def exgauss(t, t0, sigma, tau, amp, base):\n    \"\"\"Exponentially-modified Gaussian (Gaussian(sigma) convolved one-sided exp(-t/tau)).\n\n    ``t0`` is the centre of the intrinsic Gaussian = the scattering-deconvolved arrival time.\n    Numerically stable piecewise: erfcx(z)=exp(z^2)erfc(z) keeps the rising edge (z>=0) from\n    overflowing, while the scattering tail (z<0, where erfcx itself overflows) uses the direct\n    exp*erfc form whose exponent is then small.\n    \"\"\"\n    sigma = abs(sigma) + 1e-12\n    tau = abs(tau) + 1e-12\n    dt = np.asarray(t, float) - t0\n    z = (sigma / tau - dt / sigma) / np.sqrt(2.0)\n    out = np.empty(np.broadcast(dt, z).shape, float)\n    pos = z >= 0\n    out[pos] = np.exp(-0.5 * (dt[pos] / sigma) ** 2) * erfcx(z[pos])\n    a = np.clip(0.5 * (sigma / tau) ** 2 - dt[~pos] / tau, -700.0, 700.0)\n    out[~pos] = np.exp(a) * erfc(z[~pos])\n    return base + amp * out"
}

> AGENT

4 of 7 pass now — including both scattered cases and the non-detection/calibration tests. The 3 failures are all **τ=0** (no scattering): a 1.5 ms pulse at 1 ms sampling is only ~1.5 samples wide, so integer-sample dedispersion roll scatters it across sub-bands. That's a synthetic-test artifact — real CHIME data is at **2.56 µs** (pulses are hundreds of samples wide; integer roll is sub-µs-precise). Let me make the synthetic realistically fine-sampled rather than stress an unphysical coarse-`dt` corner.

  "content": "\"\"\"Validate the custom DM tool (dispersion/chime_dm.py) on synthetic known-truth bursts.\n\nThe injector is INDEPENDENT of the estimator: each channel profile is an intrinsic Gaussian\nnumerically convolved with a one-sided scattering exponential (NOT the module's erfcx exgauss),\nthen dispersed by the residual DM. So a pass means the tool recovers a known DM from a realistic\nscattered, dispersed, noisy waterfall — not that it agrees with its own model.\n\nCovers the regime that broke structure-max (smooth pulses, scattering tails, low S/N), a wide\nreference-independent offset (de-circularisation), a non-detection floor, and sigma calibration,\nin BOTH the CHIME (400-800 MHz) and DSA-110 (~1.28-1.53 GHz) bands.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pytest\n\nfrom dispersion.chime_dm import K_DM, measure_dm\n\n\ndef _inject(freqs, dt, n_t, dm_ref, dm_true, t0_base, sigma_ms, tau_ref_ms, snr, rng):\n    \"\"\"Waterfall (n_freq, n_t): scattered pulse dispersed by (dm_true - dm_ref).\"\"\"\n    nu_ref = freqs.max()\n    t = np.arange(n_t) * dt\n    wf = np.zeros((freqs.size, n_t))\n    ddm = dm_true - dm_ref\n    sig = sigma_ms * 1e-3\n    for j, nu in enumerate(freqs):\n        arr = t0_base + ddm * K_DM * (1.0 / nu**2 - 1.0 / nu_ref**2)\n        g = np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - arr) / sig) ** 2)\n        tau = tau_ref_ms * 1e-3 * (nu / nu_ref) ** -4\n        if tau > 1e-6:\n            k = np.exp(-np.arange(0, 8 * tau, dt) / tau)\n            g = np.convolve(g, k, mode=\"full\")[:n_t]\n        wf[j] = snr * g / (g.max() + 1e-12) + rng.standard_normal(n_t)\n    return wf\n\n\ndef _run(band, dm_ref, dm_off, tau_ref_ms, snr=4.0, seed=0, dm_window=50.0):\n    \"\"\"Size the window to the residual sweep, inject, and measure. ``band`` = (f_lo, f_hi).\"\"\"\n    flo, fhi = band\n    freqs = np.linspace(flo, fhi, 96)\n    dt = 2.0e-4  # 0.2 ms — pulses well resolved (real CHIME is 2.56 us; DSA finer still)\n    sweep = abs(dm_off) * K_DM * (1.0 / flo**2 - 1.0 / fhi**2)  # s, full band\n    pad = sweep + 0.1\n    n_t = int((2 * pad + 0.2) / dt)\n    t0_base = pad + 0.05\n    wf = _inject(freqs, dt, n_t, dm_ref, dm_ref + dm_off, t0_base, 1.5, tau_ref_ms, snr,\n                 np.random.default_rng(seed))\n    return measure_dm(wf, freqs, dt, dm_ref, dm_window=dm_window, dm_step=1.0)\n\n\nCHIME = (400.0, 800.0)\nDSA = (1281.0, 1531.0)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"band,dm_ref\", [(CHIME, 500.0), (DSA, 500.0)], ids=[\"chime\", \"dsa\"]\n)\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"dm_off,tau_ref_ms\", [(5.0, 0.0), (-8.0, 0.0), (12.0, 2.0), (-15.0, 5.0)]\n)\ndef test_recovers_known_dm(band, dm_ref, dm_off, tau_ref_ms):\n    res = _run(band, dm_ref, dm_off, tau_ref_ms, snr=4.0)\n    assert res[\"constrains_dm\"], f\"should constrain: {res['reason']} (n={res['n_good_subbands']})\"\n    assert abs(res[\"dm\"] - (dm_ref + dm_off)) < max(3.0 * res[\"dm_err\"], 2.0), (\n        f\"dm={res['dm']:.2f} truth={dm_ref + dm_off} sigma={res['dm_err']:.2f}\"\n    )\n\n\ndef test_wide_search_finds_large_offset_decircularizes():\n    # a +30 pc/cm^3 offset from the reference must be FOUND, not pinned at dm_ref -> the agreement\n    # test is a real exclusion, not a circular delta~0.\n    res = _run(CHIME, 500.0, 30.0, 0.0, snr=4.0)\n    assert res[\"constrains_dm\"], res[\"reason\"]\n    assert abs(res[\"dm\"] - 530.0) < max(3.0 * res[\"dm_err\"], 2.0), f\"dm={res['dm']:.2f} (want 530)\"\n\n\ndef test_flags_nondetection_at_low_snr():\n    # per-channel S/N ~1: nothing clears the floor -> not constrained, not fabricated\n    res = _run(CHIME, 500.0, 10.0, 0.0, snr=0.7, seed=1)\n    assert not res[\"constrains_dm\"]\n    assert res[\"dm\"] is None or res[\"dm_err\"] is None\n\n\ndef test_dsa_narrow_band_has_larger_sigma_but_recovers():\n    # DSA's tiny dispersive lever arm (~25x worse than CHIME) -> honest, larger sigma_DM.\n    chime = _run(CHIME, 500.0, 6.0, 1.0, snr=6.0, seed=3)\n    dsa = _run(DSA, 500.0, 6.0, 1.0, snr=6.0, seed=3)\n    assert chime[\"constrains_dm\"] and dsa[\"constrains_dm\"]\n    assert dsa[\"dm_err\"] > chime[\"dm_err\"], f\"dsa sigma {dsa['dm_err']:.2f} !> chime {chime['dm_err']:.2f}\"\n\n\ndef test_sigma_is_calibrated_across_realizations():\n    pulls = []\n    for s in range(12):\n        res = _run(CHIME, 500.0, 10.0, 1.0, snr=6.0, seed=100 + s)\n        if res[\"constrains_dm\"]:\n            pulls.append((res[\"dm\"] - 510.0) / res[\"dm_err\"])\n    assert len(pulls) >= 8, f\"too few constrained fits ({len(pulls)}/12)\"\n    assert np.std(pulls) < 3.0, f\"pull scatter {np.std(pulls):.2f} — sigma over-confident\"\n"
}

    enable_time_domain_flagging: false
    time_threshold_sigma: 7.0

    num_subbands: 4
    max_lag_mhz: 5.0
    use_snr_subbanding: true
    enable_intra_pulse_analysis: false
    intra_pulse_time_bins: 8
  fitting:

    reference_frequency_mhz: 600.0
    force_model: null
  baseline_subtraction:
    enable: true
    poly_order: 1
  noise:
    disable: false
    disable_template: false
    template_n_draws: 25
  self_noise:

# telescopes.yaml
#
# Store *raw* instrumental parameters for each facility in **one place**.
# Add as many telescope blocks as you like, one per key.  All values are
# plain numbers (SI units noted in comments); use YAML “null” (or leave
# blank) as a placeholder until you know the number.

# Example entry — DELETE or edit:
# VLA:
#   df_MHz_raw: 2.0          # native channel width [MHz]
#   dt_ms_raw: 1.0           # native time sample  [ms]
#   f_min_GHz: 1.0           # bottom of processed band [GHz]
#   f_max_GHz: 2.0           # top of processed band    [GHz]

# Telescope parameters
dsa:
  df_MHz_raw: 0.03051757812 # float, MHz
  dt_ms_raw: 32.768e-3 # float, ms
  f_min_GHz: 1.31125 # float, GHz
  f_max_GHz: 1.49875 # float, GHz
  flux_jy_per_unit: fluxcal # "fluxcal" => data-driven model-based radiometer fluence (analysis/flux_cal.joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz); DSA measured beam + coherent-beam SEFD. null => uncalibrated. See analysis/burst_energies/CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md
  beam_model_h5: null # path to the measured Jones beam cube (DSA110_beam_1.h5, ~345 MB, external/gitignored) used by analysis/dsa_beam.py for G(theta,phi,nu). SEFD is measured per-epoch by dsa110-rt (lxd110h23:5777), not stored here.
  freq_descending: true # DSA .npy stored row 0 = f_max: dsa110-scat dedisperses with fch1=1498.75 (ch0=high) and its fitter flips the model (burstfittools.py:160) to match descending data; loader flips to ascending

chime:
  df_MHz_raw: 0.390625 # float, MHz
  dt_ms_raw: 2.56e-3 # float, ms (voltage sample rate)

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/home/ubuntu/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/dispersion/chime_dm.py",
  "old_string": "    w = 1.0 / np.array(sub_err) ** 2\n    X = np.vstack([x, np.ones_like(x)]).T\n    cov = np.linalg.inv(X.T @ (X * w[:, None]))\n    slope, _c = cov @ ((X * w[:, None]).T @ np.array(sub_t0))\n    dm_err = float(np.sqrt(abs(cov[0, 0])))\n    dm = float(coarse_dm + slope)",
  "new_string": "    t0 = np.array(sub_t0)\n    w = 1.0 / np.array(sub_err) ** 2\n    X = np.vstack([x, np.ones_like(x)]).T\n    cov = np.linalg.inv(X.T @ (X * w[:, None]))\n    beta = cov @ ((X * w[:, None]).T @ t0)\n    slope = beta[0]\n    # inflate the formal (stat-only) covariance by the reduced chi^2 of the linear fit: if the\n    # sub-band arrival times scatter more than their fit errors (profile evolution, scattering,\n    # bandpass) sigma_DM grows honestly — avoids the over-confident stat-only error.\n    resid = t0 - X @ beta\n    dof = max(x.size - 2, 1)\n    chi2_red = float(np.sum(w * resid**2) / dof)\n    dm_err = float(np.sqrt(abs(cov[0, 0]) * max(chi2_red, 1.0)))\n    dm = float(coarse_dm + slope)"
}

> AGENT

Done — the custom DM tool is built, validated, and committed (`feat/custom-dm-tool`, `91651df`).

## Works on DSA data — demonstrated on real data
Ran it on a real DSA-110 burst (`phineas_dsa`, 6144×5121, catalog DM 610.274):
- **DM = 610.206 ± 0.006, S/N 140, 7/8 sub-bands, constrained** — recovers the catalog DM.

Plus 12 synthetic tests pass in **both** bands (CHIME 400–800 *and* DSA 1281–1531 MHz): known-DM recovery across τ∈{0,2,5 ms}, wide-search recovery of a +30 offset (de-circularization), non-detection floor at S/N~1, DSA σ > CHIME σ (narrow-band lever arm), and σ calibration. The injector is independent of the estimator's model, so a pass means real recovery, not self-agreement.

## What the tool does (vs the broken structure-max)
1. **Wide reference-independent incoherent DM search** → coarse DM (so a real offset is *found*, not pinned at the reference — de-circularizes the agreement test).
2. **Scatter-corrected arrival-time regression**: per sub-band, fit an exp-modified Gaussian; its center `t0` is the scattering-deconvolved arrival time → weighted linear fit of `t0` vs ν⁻² → slope = DM, χ²-inflated covariance = honest σ. Low S/N → `constrains_dm=False`, no fabrication.

Pure numpy/scipy, no flits deps — the *same* module runs in the baseband docker image and on host (no more vendored-copy drift).

**One honest caveat:** the reported σ is statistical; phineas's 0.07 pc/cm³ offset from catalog is physically negligible but ~10σ on σ_stat alone. So the **agreement test needs a ~1 pc/cm³ physical floor** (per the expert) — that belongs in the pillar-2 logic, not the estimator.

**Remaining (P4):** docker-extract all 12 CHIME singlebeam bursts with this tool, classify constrains/doesn't, wire the agreement test with the floor, regenerate the report, un-null the constrained DMs, and PR. That's a ~30–60 min docker run. Want me to kick it off now, or review the tool first?

  "old_string": "def _dedisperse(wf, freqs, dt, ddm, nu_ref):\n    \"\"\"Incoherently shift each channel by the dispersive delay of a residual DM ``ddm``.\"\"\"\n    shifts = np.round(K_DM * ddm * (1.0 / freqs**2 - 1.0 / nu_ref**2) / dt).astype(int)\n    return np.array([np.roll(wf[j], -shifts[j]) for j in range(freqs.size)])",
  "new_string": "def _dedisperse(wf, freqs, dt, ddm, nu_ref):\n    \"\"\"Incoherently shift each channel by the dispersive delay of a residual DM ``ddm``.\n\n    Zero-fills the shifted-in edge (does NOT wrap): a short recording window (e.g. a ~143 ms CHIME\n    singlebeam) would otherwise wrap a large shift back into the burst and fake an alignment.\n    \"\"\"\n    shifts = np.round(K_DM * ddm * (1.0 / freqs**2 - 1.0 / nu_ref**2) / dt).astype(int)\n    out = np.zeros_like(wf)\n    n = wf.shape[1]\n    for j, s in enumerate(shifts):\n        if abs(s) >= n:\n            continue\n        if s > 0:\n            out[j, : n - s] = wf[j, s:]\n        elif s < 0:\n            out[j, -s:] = wf[j, : n + s]\n        else:\n            out[j] = wf[j]\n    return out"
}
